about.title: Cudahy Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Cudahy is a small, tightly packed city, and its stores, apartment complexes, and sidewalks along corridors like Atlantic Avenue and Clara Street see steady foot traffic every day. When a property owner or manager lets a spill, broken step, uneven walkway, or poor lighting go unaddressed, a quick trip to the store can turn into a serious injury. California law requires the injured person to show the owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard and failed to fix it or warn visitors. That means what happens in the hours after a fall matters: photos of the hazard, names of witnesses, and requests to preserve surveillance footage can all shape a claim. We handle premises liability claims and will review your situation at no upfront cost to explain your options.

whyChoose.title: Why Choose Us for Your Fall Claim

items.title: We Understand the Notice Requirement
items.desc: California premises claims hinge on proving the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. Our team knows how to dig into maintenance logs, prior complaints, and inspection records to build that case.

items.title: We Push for Video Before It's Erased
items.desc: Many stores and apartment buildings overwrite surveillance footage within days or weeks. Getting our team involved quickly can mean the difference between having proof of the hazard and having none.

items.title: We Know Pure Comparative Fault Cuts Both Ways
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover damages even if you were partly at fault, though your share of blame reduces the amount. Our team can help make sure your own conduct isn't unfairly overstated by the property owner's insurer.

items.question: I fell at a store in Cudahy but didn't take photos right away. Is it too late?
items.answer: It's not too late, but time matters because conditions change and surveillance video may be deleted after a set retention period. We can send a preservation letter quickly to the property owner or manager. Even without photos, witness statements, incident reports, and store records can still help establish what happened.

items.question: How long do I have to file a premises liability claim in California?
items.answer: Generally you have two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit, though if a government-owned property is involved — like a public sidewalk or building — the deadline to act can be much shorter. Because Cudahy has a mix of private businesses and public spaces along streets like Wilcox Avenue and Santa Ana Street, it's worth having us confirm which timeline applies to your situation early.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: No. Our team reviews your situation at no cost, and we work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront fee to have your case evaluated.
